title: Against Eckhardus twisting Beza and Piscator; Moses' seeming contradictions are not two wills in God
pass_a_gloss: Henry Eckhardus little candidly thrusts a contrary opinion upon our men in fascicle 1 q.2, twisting the words of Beza and of Piscator: that God sometimes by the word signifies that he wills what he does not truly will, or that he does not will what he truly wills. To which great men the words of Moses Gen. 22, Exod. 9 and 10 and 4 gave occasion of so speaking — not that they attribute truly contrary wills to God, nor that they hostilely commit the internal concept of God with his external word. Far be it that our Doctors thrust this upon the scriptures or sense so wrongly of God! There is only an apparent-opposition in the words of Moses, arisen from this: that God through the word indeed always signifies that he wills something which he truly wills; yet he does not always signify that he precisely wills that which we conceive him to will at first sight.
pass_b_english: Henry Eckhardus unfairly foists a contrary opinion on our teachers (Fasciculus 1.q.2), twisting Beza's words and Piscator's — that God sometimes by the Word signifies He wills what He does not truly will, or refuses what He truly wills.

Those great men took occasion from Moses' words ([[Genesis 22:2 >> Bible:Genesis 22:2]], [[Genesis 22:12 >> Bible:Genesis 22:12]]; [[Exodus 9:1 >> Bible:Exodus 9:1]], [[Exodus 9:12 >> Bible:Exodus 9:12]]; [[Exodus 10:20 >> Bible:Exodus 10:20]]; [[Exodus 4:21 >> Bible:Exodus 4:21]]) — not to ascribe truly contrary wills to God. Far be it from our doctors to charge the Scriptures with that! There is only an apparent opposition (ἐναντιοφάνεια) in Moses' words: God always signifies by the Word that He wills something He truly wills; He does not always signify that He precisely wills what we first imagine Him to will. If Eckhardus wants to be a fair interpreter, let him learn candor.
source_text:
Contrariam opinionem Henricus Eckhardus nostris parum candide impingit fasciculi sui cap.1. q.2. detorquens verba Bezae… Et Piscatoris… Deum interdum verbo significare se velle, quod revera non vult; aut nolle, quod revera vult.

Quibus magnis viris occasionem ita loquendi praebuere verba Mosis Gen. 22.2.12., Exod. 9.1.12. & cap. 10.20. & 4.21. non ut vere contrarias voluntates Deo tribuant… Est duntaxat in verbis Mosis ἐναντιοφάνεια inde ortum, quod Deus per verbum quidem semper significet, se aliquid velle, quod vere vult; non tamen semper significet, se id praecise velle, quod nos eum velle prima fronte concipimus.
